outcome: THRESHOLD B DOES NOT CLOSE AND STAYS AT ONE. The webhook architecture is SELECTED and its code branch is PROVEN for the first time since §294 rewrote the dispatcher. The destination itself does not exist and could not be created: no monitored receiver is available through already-authorised access, and inventing, faking or under-monitoring one were each forbidden and would each have reproduced MO-2 with a different cause.

architecture.rationale: Not cost and not speed. The product name is to be replaced before external beta, and a verified sending domain entrenches a name — the domain, its DNS, its warmed sending reputation and every address on it — whereas a webhook URL is one environment variable to replace.
architecture.consequence: EM-2 stays OPEN and is not partially satisfied. A webhook cannot deliver a password-reset link. Transactional email waits for the brand decision or for Threshold C, whichever comes first.
architecture.configurationSurface: OPERATIONAL_ALERT_WEBHOOK_URL — one server-side Render variable. The URL is the credential: the dispatcher sends no auth header, so it must never appear in frontend-next, in any NEXT_PUBLIC_* variable, in Preview, in source control or in an evidence file. Record its host, never its path.

webhookBranchProof.whyItWasNeeded: §291 and §292 proved the webhook branch against a local receiver BEFORE §294 rewrote the dispatcher, and §294 proved the new outcome machinery entirely on the EMAIL branch — the string "webhook" does not appear in test-294-monitoring-email-channel.ts. At the moment the architecture was selected, the webhook branch outcome recording had never been executed by anything. Closing MO-1 on an unexercised code path would have been the same kind of assumption MO-2 was.
webhookBranchProof.separateFileRationale: A separate file rather than four more cases in the §294 gate: §294 records 21/21 and is cited in the register, and editing it to say something else would rewrite a finished result to describe work it did not do.

webhook takes precedence when both channels are configured

dedupe and the hard ceiling hold on the webhook channel

webhookBranchProof.deliberateAsymmetry: The webhook branch does NOT apply the email branch MALFORMED_RESPONSE rule. An arbitrary receiver has no acknowledgement schema, so 2xx IS the acknowledgement. A dispatcher demanding a JSON acknowledgement would report every successful Slack delivery as a failure. Recorded as a decision (case W-ASYM) rather than left to read as an oversight.
webhookBranchProof.wirePayloadMeasured: A payload carrying a planted observation text, a planted Authorization header and a planted API key transmitted the identifiers and [redacted], and none of the three planted strings.
webhookBranchProof.harnessBugFoundAndFixed: The first run failed W3: a 204 came back as NETWORK_FAILURE. The cause was the harness — new Response("", {status:204}) throws, because a 204 has a null body by definition — and the product had behaved correctly by classifying a thrown fetch as a transport failure. Fixing it turned a harness bug into the most operationally relevant case in the file, since 204 is what a real Discord webhook returns. Recorded rather than quietly corrected.
webhookBranchProof.antiVacuity: Case W-AV: a receiver 404 now yields PROVIDER_REJECTED with a warning-severity line; before §294 this exact case produced no observation, no event and no readiness change — the webhook simply stopped working silently.

destinationSearch.whyEachShortcutIsTheSameDefect: Every one of them yields /health/ready reporting alerting CONFIGURED over nothing watching. That is MO-2 with a different cause. Three sections were spent making that state impossible to reach by accident; reaching it on purpose to close a gate would have been worse.
destinationSearch.alsoRejected: A receiver inside the Safety InSite stack itself — a monitoring destination that dies with the thing it monitors is not a monitoring destination.

liveMO1Proof.reason: no destination exists, so there was nothing to prove receipt against. The runbook step that induces a qualifying production failure was deliberately NOT run: inducing a production 500 to watch an alert go nowhere would have degraded production for no evidence.

noiseAndDedupe.reason: the configuration did not change, so there was no change whose effect on production behaviour needed re-measuring. The §295 production re-proof (404/401/401/400 -> serverErrorsInWindow 0) remains the current live evidence, and §296 re-proved the full policy against the deployed code path locally, including five real 500s through the real ServerErrorAlertFilter raising exactly one alert and one send.

failureContainment: PRESERVED AND RE-PROVEN on the webhook branch: a receiver that throws leaves the primary operation completed, nothing thrown, 0 unhandled rejections, and the alert genuinely attempted and genuinely failed.
